words.definition: verb: to reveal or make known something, usually unintentionally
words.example: With the gold medal at stake, the gymnast awaited his turn, his quivering lip betraying his intense emotions.

words.definition: verb: to object or show reluctance
words.example: Wallace disliked the cold, so he demurred when his friends suggested they go skiing in the Alps.

words.definition: adjective: lacking
words.example: She did not think her vocabulary was wanting, yet there were so many words that inevitably she found a few she didn't know.

words.definition: verb: to give a false representation to; misrepresent
words.example: The smile on her face belies the pain she must feel after the death of her husband.

words.definition: verb: to respect deeply
words.example: The professor, despite his sleep-inducing lectures, was venerated amongst his colleagues, publishing more papers yearly than all of his peers combined.

words.definition: adjective: spending resources recklessly or wastefully
words.example: The composer Wagner, while living on a limited salary, was so profligate as to line all the walls of his apartment with pure silk.

words.definition: adjective: to be likely to socialize with others
words.example: Often we think that great leaders are those who are gregarious, always in the middle of a large group of people; yet, as Mahatma Gandhi and many others have shown us, leaders can also be introverted.

words.definition: adjective: not spending much money (but spending wisely)
words.example: Monte was no miser, but was simply frugal, wisely spending the little that he earned.

words.definition: adjective: standing out in a negative way; shockingly bad
words.example: The dictator’s abuse of human rights was so egregious that many world leaders demanded that he be tried in an international court for genocide.

words.definition: adjective: harmless and doesn’t produce any ill effects
words.example: Everyone found Nancy’s banter innocuous—except for Mike, who felt like she was intentionally picking on him.

words.definition: noun: bitterness and ill will
words.example: The acrimony between the president and vice-president sent a clear signal to voters: the health of the current administration was imperiled.

words.definition: adjective: (describes a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words
words.example: While Martha always swooned over the hunky, laconic types in romantic comedies, her boyfriends inevitably were very talkative—and not very hunky.

words.definition: adjective: being disrespectful; improperly forward or bold
words.example: Dexter, distraught over losing his pet dachshund, Madeline, found the police officer’s questions impertinent—after all, he thought, did she have to pry into such details as to what Madeline’s favorite snack was?

words.definition: verb: to weaken (usually paired with an abstract term)
words.example: The student undermined the teacher’s authority by questioning the teacher’s judgment on numerous occasions.

words.definition: verb: to suggest something subtly
words.example: At first Manfred’s teachers intimated to his parents that he was not suited to skip a grade; when his parents protested, teachers explicitly told them that, notwithstanding the boy’s precocity, he was simply too immature to jump to the 6th grade.

words.definition: adjective: exhibiting artistic skill
words.example: Picasso is generally considered the most artful member of the Cubist movement.

words.definition: adjective: favorable, the opposite of sinister
words.example: Despite an auspicious beginning, Mike’s road trip became a series of mishaps, and he was soon stranded and penniless, leaning against his wrecked automobile.

words.definition: noun: making of a false statement meant to injure a person’s reputation
words.example: With the presidential primaries well under way, the air is thick with calumny, and the mud already waist-high.

words.definition: verb: to assert
words.example: The scientist maintained that the extinction of dinosaurs was most likely brought about by a drastic change in climate.

words.definition: verb: to sap energy from
words.example: John preferred to avoid equatorial countries; the intense sun would always leave him enervated after he’d spent the day sightseeing.

words.definition: adjective: (of a person) prone to unexpected and unpredictable changes in mood
words.example: The fact that Ella’s moods were as mercurial as the weather was problematic for her relationships—it didn’t help that she lived in Chicago.

words.definition: verb: to reprimand harshly
words.example: Drill sergeants are known to castigate new recruits so mercilessly that the latter often break down during their first week in training.

words.definition: adjective: to be naïve and innocent
words.example: Two-years in Manhattan had changed Jenna from an ingenuous girl from the suburbs to a jaded urbanite, unlikely to fall for any ruse, regardless of how elaborate.

words.definition: verb: to make less severe; to limit (a statement)
words.example: Chris qualified his love for San Francisco, adding he didn't like the weather there as much as he liked the weather in Los Angeles.

words.definition: verb: to reprimand harshly
words.example: Though chastised for eating the snacks for the party, Lawrence shrugged off his mother’s harsh words, and continued to plow through jars of cookies and boxes of donuts.

words.definition: adjective: easily persuaded
words.example: Even though she did not like the outdoors, Shirley was generally amenable and so her brother was able to persuade her to go camping.

words.definition: adjective: mixed or conflicting emotions about something
words.example: Sam was ambivalent about studying for the exam because doing so ate up a lot of his time, yet he was able to improve his analytical skills.

words.definition: adjective: extremely frugal; miserly
words.example: Katie is so parsimonious that she only buys a pair of socks if all of her other socks have holes in them.

words.definition: adjective: confusing or ambiguous
words.example: The findings of the study were equivocal—the two researchers had different opinions on what the results signified.

words.definition: noun: a deviation from what is normal or expected
words.example: Aberrations in climate have become the norm: rarely a week goes by without some meteorological phenomenon making headlines.

words.definition: adjective: open to more than one interpretation
words.example: The coach told his team, “Move towards that side of the field”; because he did not point, his directions were ambiguous, and the team had no idea to which side he was referring.

words.definition: adjective: still in existence (usually refers to documents).
words.example: Despite many bookstores closing, experts predict that some form of book dealing will still be extant generations from now.

words.definition: noun: a mixture of multiple things
words.example: The band’s music was an amalgam of hip-hop, flamenco and jazz, blending the three styles with surprising results.

words.definition: verb: to express strong disapproval
words.example: After being caught in bed with a mistress, the mayor was quickly censured by the city council.

words.definition: adjective: narrowly restricted in scope or outlook
words.example: Jasmine was sad to admit it, but her fledgling relationship with Jacob did not work out because his culinary tastes were simply too parochial; "After all," she quipped on her blog, "he considered Chef Boyardee ethnic food."

words.definition: verb: to clear of accusation, blame, suspicion, or doubt with supporting arguments or proof
words.example: Even seven Tour de France wins cannot vindicate Lance Armstrong in the eyes of the public--that the athlete used performance enhancing drugs invalidates all those wins.

words.definition: adjective: unbiased; neutral
words.example: The potential juror knew the defendant, and therefore could not serve on the jury, which must consist only of disinterested members.

words.definition: adjective: restless
words.example: The crowd grew restive as the comedian’s opening jokes fell flat.

words.definition: adjective: complicated, and difficult to comprehend
words.example: The physics lecture became so involved that the undergraduate’s eyes glazed over.

words.definition: noun: somebody who attacks cherished beliefs or institutions
words.example: Lady Gaga, in challenging what it means to be clothed, is an iconoclast for wearing a "meat dress" to a prominent awards show.

words.definition: verb: to excite or inspire (someone) to action
words.example: At mile 23 of his first marathon, Kyle had all but given up, until he noticed his friends and family holding a banner that read, “Go Kyle”; galvanized, he broke into a gallop, finishing the last three miles in less than 20 minutes.

words.definition: noun: a long pompous speech; a tirade
words.example: Dinner at Billy's was more a punishment than a reward, since anyone who sat at the dinner table would have to listen to Billy's father's interminable harangues against the government.

words.definition: noun: the condition of being susceptible to bribes or corruption
words.example: Even some of the most sacred sporting events are not immune to venality, as many of the officials have received substantial bribes to make biased calls.

words.definition: adjective: to be in proportion or corresponding in degree or amount
words.example: The convicted felon’s life sentence was commensurate with the heinousness of his crime.

words.definition: adjective: truthful
words.example: While we elect our leaders in the hope that every word they speak  will be veracious, history has shown that such a hope is naive.

words.definition: adjective: not normal
words.example: According to those who do not believe in climate change, the extreme weather over the last five years is simply anomalous—daily temperatures should return to their old averages, they believe.

words.definition: adjective: shapeless
words.example: His study plan for the GRE was at best amorphous; he would do questions from random pages in any one of seven test prep books.

words.definition: verb: to speak in an evasive way
words.example: The cynic quipped, “There is not much variance in politicians; they all seem to prevaricate”.

words.definition: verb: to reproach; to scold
words.example: Bob took a risk walking into the "Students Barbershop"—in the end he had to upbraid the apparently drunk barber for giving him an uneven bowl cut.

words.definition: adjective: rashly or wastefully extravagant
words.example: Successful professional athletes who do not fall prey to prodigality seem to be the exception—most live decadent lives.

words.definition: verb: criticize severely or angrily
words.example: Showing no patience, the manager utterly lambasted the sales team that lost the big account.

words.definition: adjective: improperly forward or bold
words.example: In an impudent move, the defendant spoke out of order to say terribly insulting things to the judge.

words.definition: adjective: difficult to penetrate; incomprehensible to one of ordinary understanding or knowledge
words.example: I found Ulysses recondite and never finished the book, waiting instead to read it with someone else so we could penetrate its meaning together.

words.definition: adjective: characterized by unusual lightness and delicacy
words.example: The gossamer wings of a butterfly, which allow it to fly, are also a curse, so delicate that they are often damaged.

words.definition: verb: make less severe or harsh
words.example: I can only spend so much time mitigating your disagreements with your wife, and at certain point, you need to do it on your own.

words.definition: adjective: impossible to stop or prevent
words.example: The rise of the computer was an inexorable shift in technology and culture.

words.definition: noun: a trite or obvious remark
words.example: The professor argued that many statements regarded as wise in previous times, such as the Golden Rule, are now regarded as mere platitudes.

words.definition: adjective: occurring by happy chance; having no cause or apparent cause
words.example: Missing my train turned out to be quite fortuitous since I ran into a childhood friend on the next train and we were able to reconnect after so many years.

words.definition: noun: the power to foresee the future
words.example: Baxter's warnings about investing in technology stocks seemed like an act of prescience after the whole market declined significantly.

words.definition: verb: make worse
words.example: Her sleeplessness exacerbated her cold--when she woke up the next day, her sinuses were completely blocked.

words.definition: noun: a strong liking
words.example: Monte had a predilection for the fine things in life: Cuban cigars, 200 dollar bottles of wine, and trips to the French Riviera.

words.definition: adjective: habitually complaining
words.example: The querulous old woman was beginning to wear down even the happier members of the staff with her ceaseless complaining.

words.definition: verb: avoid and stay away from deliberately; stay clear of
words.example: Politicians are the masters of eschewing morals; academics are the masters of eschewing clarity.

words.definition: adjective: relating to the pleasant aspects of the country
words.example: The noble families of England once owned vast expanses of beautiful, bucolic land.

words.definition: adjective: showing modest reserve; lacking self-confidence
words.example: As a young girl she was diffident and reserved, but now as an adult, she is confident and assertive.

words.definition: verb: make unclear
words.example: On the Smith's drive through the Grand Canyon, Mr. Smith's big head obscured much of Mrs. Robinson's view, so that she only saw momentary patches of red rock.

words.definition: adjective: mysterious or vague, usually intentionally
words.example: Since Sarah did not want her husband to guess the Christmas present she had bought him, she only answered cryptically when he would ask her questions about it.

words.definition: adjective: expecting unquestioning obedience; characteristic of an absolute ruler
words.example: The coach was dictatorial in his approach: no players could ever argue or question his approach.

words.definition: verb: reach the highest or most decisive point
words.example: Beethoven's musical genius culminated in the 9th Symphony, which many consider his greatest work.

words.definition: noun: a state of guilt
words.example: Since John had left his banana peel at the top of the stairwell, he accepted culpability for Martha's broken leg.

words.definition: adjective: overly sentimental to the point that it is disgusting
words.example: The film was incredibly mawkish, introducing highly likeable characters only to have them succumb to a devastating illness by the end of the movie.

words.definition: adjective: marked by a lack of interest
words.example: Mr. Thompson was so talented at teaching math that even normally apathetic students took interest.

words.definition: noun: the quality of talking or writing easily and continuously
words.example: The professor's volubility knows no bounds; he could talk through a hurricane and elaborate a point from one St. Patrick's Day to the next.

words.definition: adjective: highly opinionated, not accepting that one's own beliefs may not be correct
words.example: Bryan is dogmatic in his belief that the earth is flat, claiming that all pictures of a spherical earth are computer generated.

words.definition: verb: to chuckle, laugh merrily, often in a breathy, muffled way
words.example: Walking into the cafe, I could hear happy, chortling people and smell the rich aroma of roasted coffee beans.

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of rural life; awkwardly simple and provincial
words.example: The vacation cabin had no electricity and no indoor plumbing, but despite these inconveniences, Nigel adored its rustic charm.

words.definition: verb: keep from happening or arising; make impossible
words.example: The manager specified that all other gates be locked, to preclude the possibility of persons without tickets entering the arena undetected.

words.definition: adjective: having or demonstrating ability to recognize or draw fine distinctions
words.example: The lawyer had an incisive mind, able in a flash to dissect a hopelessly tangled issue and isolate the essential laws at play.

words.definition: adjective: disinclined to talk, not revealing one's thoughts
words.example: When asked about her father, Helen lost her outward enthusiasm and became rather reticent.

words.definition: adjective: showing respect
words.example: If you ever have the chance to meet the president, stand up straight and be deferential.

words.definition: adjective: instructive (especially excessively)
words.example: Tolstoy's The Death of Ivan Ilyich is a didactic novel, instructing the reader on how to live a good life.

words.definition: adjective: fixed firmly or securely
words.example: By the time we reach 60-years old, most of our habits are so entrenched that it is difficult for us to change.

words.definition: adjective: repeated too often; overfamiliar through overuse
words.example: The professor used such banal expression that many students in the class either fell asleep from boredom or stayed awake to complete his sentences and humor friends.

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme care in treatment of details
words.example: The Japanese noodle maker was meticulous in making his noodles and would never let another person take over the task.

words.definition: noun: inactivity resulting from lethargy and lack of vigor or energy
words.example: After work, I was expecting my colleagues to be enthusiastic about the outing, but I found them in a state of complete torpor.

words.definition: adjective: relevant and appropriate
words.example: The professor wanted to tell the jury in detail about his new book, but the lawyer said it wasn't germane to the charges in the cases.

words.definition: adjective: serving no useful purpose
words.example: How can we hope to stay open if we don't eliminate all superfluous spending, like catered meetings and free acupuncture Tuesday?

words.definition: adjective: characterized by good taste in manners and conduct
words.example: Sally's parties are decorous affairs, and instead of the usual beer and music, there is tea and intellectual conversation.

words.definition: noun: one who professes great sensitivity to the beauty of art and nature
words.example: A true aesthete, Marty would spend hours at the Guggenheim Museum, staring at the same Picasso.

words.definition: adjective: willing to be bold in social situations or to take risks
words.example: As all of the other campers cowered in their tents, Bill, armed only with a flashlight, audaciously tracked down the bear that had raided their food.

words.definition: adjective: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious
words.example: Among the tall trees and flower fields, the building seemed out of place with its conspicuous, cold concrete and angular steel exterior.

words.definition: noun: the trait of being rude and impertinent
words.example: The speeding car had the gall to switch five lanes at once, run through a red light, and then cut off a police car before finally coming to a stop in front of a sea of flashing red lights.

words.definition: adjective: not serious in content or attitude or behavior
words.example: Compared to Juliet's passionate concern for human rights, Jake's non-stop concern about football seems somewhat frivolous.

words.definition: verb: acknowledge defeat
words.example: I concede. You win!

words.definition: noun: an excessive supply
words.example: The Internet offers such a glut of news related stories that many find it difficult to know which story to read first.

words.definition: verb: give rise to
words.example: The restrictions of the Treaty of Versailles were so severe that they engendered deep hatred and resentment in the German people.

words.definition: verb: deny or contradict; speak against or oppose
words.example: I can't gainsay a single piece of evidence James has presented, but I still don't trust his conclusion.

words.definition: noun: an act of deliberate betrayal; a breach of a trust
words.example: Sure, he was the best salesman in the company; but Michael had abused the trust of the firm, sharing product secrets with a competitor, and for such perfidy he was terminated.

words.definition: adjective: conspicuously and offensively loud; given to vehement outcry
words.example: In giving Marcia a particular vociferous response, Paul caused people at every other table in the restaurant to turn around and look at them angrily.

words.definition: adjective: concerned with the appreciation of beauty
words.example: The director, not known for his aesthetic sensibilities, decided not to use costumes at all, and put on the play in everyday clothing.

words.definition: verb: describe in detail
words.example: After a brief summary of proper swimming technique, the coach delineated the specifics of each stroke, spending 30 minutes alone on the backstroke.

words.definition: verb: to make someone who is angry less angry; placate
words.example: In the morning, Janine was unable to mollify Harry, if he happened to become angry, unless he'd had his cup of coffee.

words.definition: verb: make something bad better
words.example: "Three Cups of Tea" tells the story of western man who hopes to ameliorate poverty and the lack of education in Afghanistan.

words.definition: adjective: not inclined towards physical exertion or effort; slow and relaxed
words.example: As the sun beat down and the temperature climbed higher, we spent a languid week lying around the house.

words.definition: verb: hinder or prevent (the efforts, plans, or desires) of
words.example: I thought I would finish writing the paper by lunchtime, but a number of urgent interruptions served to frustrate my plan.

words.definition: adjective: so small as to be meaningless; insignificant
words.example: The GRE tests cumulative knowledge, so if you cram the night before it is, at best, likely to only have a negligible impact on your score.

words.definition: verb: be a sign or indication of; have as a meaning
words.example: Even if the text is not visible, the red octagon denotes "stop" to all motorists in America.

words.definition: verb: come from; be connected by a relationship of blood, for example
words.example: Many words in the English language are derived from Latin, including the word "derive."

words.definition: adjective: being essentially equal to something
words.example: In many situations, remaining silent is tantamount to admitting guilt, so speak to prove your innocence.

words.definition: noun: an absurd presentation of something; a mockery
words.example: What I expected to be an intelligent, nuanced historical documentary turned out to be a poorly-produced travesty of the form.

words.definition: adjective: firm and dependable especially in loyalty
words.example: No longer a staunch supporter of the movement, Todd now will openly question whether its goals are worthwhile.

words.definition: adjective: found in the ordinary course of events
words.example: Phil gets so involved thinking about Aristotle's arguments that he totally forgets quotidian concerns, such as exercising and eating regularly.

words.definition: adjective: characterized by or characteristic of exceptionally early development or maturity (especially in mental aptitude)
words.example: Though only seven years old, she was a precocious chess prodigy, able to beat players twice her age.

words.definition: adjective: full of high-spirited delight because of triumph or success
words.example: My hardwork paid off, and I was jubilant to receive a perfect score on the GRE.

words.definition: adjective: tending to betray
words.example: Even though Jesse James was an outlaw, his killer, Robert Ford, is remembered more for his treacherous actions than for eliminating a criminal and murderer.

words.definition: adjective: excessively greedy
words.example: Since avaricious desire is similar to gluttony or lust--sins of excess--it was listed as one of the seven deadly sins by the Catholic church.

words.definition: verb: cleverly find a way out of one's duties or obligations
words.example: One way of circumventing the GRE is to apply to a grad school that does not require GRE scores.

words.definition: verb: spread negative information about
words.example: Todd was noble after the divorce, choosing to say only complimentary things about Barbara, but Barbara did not hesitate to vilify Todd.

words.definition: adjective: lasting a very short time
words.example: The lifespan of a mayfly is ephemeral, lasting from a few hours to a couple of days.

words.definition: verb: contain or include
words.example: The rogue wave quickly subsumed the pier and boardwalk, destroying everything in its path.

words.definition: adjective: practicing self-denial
words.example: His ascetic life is the main reason he inspired so many followers, especially since he gave up wealth and power to live in poverty.

words.definition: adjective: lacking in harmony or compatibility or appropriateness
words.example: The vast economic inequality of modern society is incongruous with America's ideals.

words.definition: adjective: admitting of no doubt or misunderstanding; having only one meaning or interpretation and leading to only one conclusion
words.example: The President's first statement on the subject was vague and open to competing interpretations, so when he spoke to Congress about the same subject later, he was careful to make his position completely unequivocal.

words.definition: adjective: standing above others in quality or position
words.example: Shakespeare is an eminent author in the English language, but I find his writing uninteresting and melodramatic.

words.definition: verb: take the place or move into the position of
words.example: For many, a cell phone has supplanted a traditional phone; in fact, most 20-somethings don't even have a traditional phone anymore.

words.definition: adjective: being in the earliest stages of development; being or involving basic facts or principles
words.example: I would love to be able to present a fully polished proposal to the board, but right now, our plans for the product are still in the most rudimentary stages.

words.definition: adjective: marked by or showing hopelessness
words.example: After her third pet dog died, Marcia was simply forlorn: this time even the possibility of buying a new dog no longer held any joy.

words.definition: adjective: comprised of a variety of styles
words.example: Malala was known for her eclectic tastes in music, one moment dancing to disco the next "air conducting" along to Beethoven's 9th symphony.

words.definition: adjective: having or showing arrogant superiority to and disdain of those one views as unworthy
words.example: The haughty manager didn't believe that any of his subordinates could ever have an insight as brilliant as his own.

words.definition: adjective: not able to be changed
words.example: Taxes are one of the immutable laws of the land, so there is no use arguing about paying them.

words.definition: adjective: stubbornly resistant to authority or control
words.example: Used to studious high school students, Martha was unprepared for the refractory Kindergarteners who neither sat still nor listened to a single word she said.

words.definition: noun: distinctive and showy elegance
words.example: Jim, with his typical panache, came to the wedding reception with a top hat and cane.

words.definition: verb: choose not to consume or take part in (particularly something enjoyable)
words.example: Considered a health nut, Jessica abstained from anything containing sugar--even chocolate.

words.definition: adjective: of a belief that is based on faulty reasoning
words.example: The widespread belief that Inuit have forty different words for "snow" has been considered fallacious, based on a single report by Anthropologist Franz Boas.

words.definition: verb: to pull off a plan or scheme, usually through skill or trickery
words.example: Despite a low GPA, he contrived to get into college, going so far as to write his own glowing letters of recommendation.

words.definition: adjective: plausible but false
words.example: When listening to a politician speak, it is hard to distinguish the spurious claims from the authentic ones.

words.definition: noun: an absence of emotion or enthusiasm
words.example: Widespread apathy among voters led to a very small turnout on election day.

words.definition: adjective: marked by extreme intensity of emotions or convictions
words.example: While the other employees responded to the bad news in a measured way, Andrew responded in a vehement manner, tipping over his desk and shouting at the top of his lungs.

words.definition: adjective: working in a subtle but destructive way
words.example: Plaque is insidious: we cannot see it, but each day it eats away at our enamel, causing cavities and other dental problems.

words.definition: adjective: not original but drawing strongly on something already in existence, especially in reference to a creative product (e.g. music, writing, poetry etc.).
words.example: Because the movies were utterly derivative of other popular movies, they did well at the box office.

words.definition: adjective: noble and generous in spirit, especially towards a rival or someone less powerful
words.example: He was a great sportsman: in defeat he was complimentary and in victory he was magnanimous.

words.definition: adjective: traveling from place to place to work
words.example: Doctors used to be itinerant, traveling between patients' homes.

words.definition: adjective: stubbornly unyielding
words.example: Even the most tenacious advocates for gun ownership must admit some of the dangers that firearms present.

words.definition: noun: a person who holds unorthodox opinions in any field (not merely religion)
words.example: Though everybody at the gym told Mikey to do cardio before weights, Mikey was a heretic and always did the reverse.

words.definition: adjective: free of deceit
words.example: At first I thought my niece was guileless, but I then found myself buying her ice cream every time we passed a shop.

words.definition: adjective: discontented as toward authority
words.example: After watching his superior take rations from the soldiers, he quickly became disaffected and rebelled.

words.definition: verb: make clearer and easier to understand
words.example: Youtube is great place to learn just about anything--an expert elucidates finer points so that even a complete novice can learn.

words.definition: verb: place side by side for contrast
words.example: The appeal of her paintings comes from a classical style which is juxtaposed with modern themes.

words.definition: noun: fanatical patriotism
words.example: North Korea maintains intense control over its population through a combination of jingoism and cult of personality.

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of one eager to fight
words.example: Tom said that he was arguing the matter purely for philosophical reasons, but his belligerent tone indicated an underlying anger about the issue.

words.definition: adjective: marked by a narrow focus on or display of learning especially its trivial aspects
words.example: Professor Thompson was regarded as an expert in his field, but his lectures were utterly pedantic, focused on rigorous details of the most trivial conventions in the field.

words.definition: adjective: markedly different from an accepted norm
words.example: When the financial director started screaming and throwing food at his co-workers, the police had to come in to deal with his aberrant behavior.

words.definition: adjective: without any attempt at concealment; completely obvious
words.example: Allen was often punished in school for blatantly disrespecting teachers.

words.definition: adjective: serving to warn; expressing reproof or reproach especially as a corrective
words.example: At the assembly, the high school vice-principal gave the students an admonitory speech, warning them of the many risks and dangers of prom night.

words.definition: adjective: refusing to change one's mind
words.example: Civil rights icon Rosa Parks will forever be remembered for adamantly refusing to give up her seat on a public bus--even after the bus driver insisted, she remained rooted in place.

words.definition: noun: the trait of seeming not to care
words.example: In an effort to fight indifference, the president of the college introduced a new, stricter grading system.

words.definition: adjective: difficult to understand; incomprehensible
words.example: Physics textbooks can seem so abstruse to the uninitiated that readers feel as though they are looking at hieroglyphics.

words.definition: adjective: requiring and demanding accuracy
words.example: Though his childhood piano teacher was so exacting, Max is thankful now, as a professional pianist.

words.definition: verb: add details or explanation; clarify the meaning; state in depth
words.example: The CEO refused to expound on the decision to merge our department with another one, and so I quit.

words.definition: adjective: harsh in tone
words.example: Most movie critics are acerbic towards summer blockbusters, often referring to them as garbage.

words.definition: noun: the trait of avoiding excesses
words.example: Welles wasn't known for his temperance--he usually ate enough for two and drank enough for three.

words.definition: adjective: lacking significance through having been overused
words.example: Cheryl rolled her eyes when she heard the lecturer's hackneyed advice to "be true to yourself."

words.definition: adjective: describing a statement that is not believable
words.example: The teacher found it implausible that the student was late to school because he had been kidnapped by outlaws on horseback.

words.definition: adjective: defying tradition or convention
words.example: Jackson Pollock was an iconoclastic artist, totally breaking with tradition by splashing paint on a blank canvas.

words.definition: verb: to completely destroy
words.example: I tried eradicating the mosquitos in my apartment with a rolled up newspaper, but there were too many of them.

words.definition: adjective: characteristic of a limited perspective; not fashionable or sophisticated
words.example: Maggie's enthusiasm about her high school teams seemed provincial to her college classmates, all of whom were following a nationally ranked college team.

words.definition: verb: interpreted in a particular way

words.example: Hundreds of years ago, Galileo was anathema to the church; today the church is anathema to some on the left side of the political spectrum.

words.definition: verb: to speak vaguely, usually with the intention to mislead or deceive
words.example: After Sharon brought the car home an hour after her curfew, she equivocated when her parents pointedly asked her where she had been.

words.definition: noun: depravity; a depraved act
words.example: During his reign, Caligula indulged in unspeakable sexual practices, so it is not surprising that he will forever be remembered for his turpitude.

words.definition: noun: a person who has abandoned a religious faith or cause
words.example: An apostate of the Orthodox faith he was raised in, Sheldon continues to seek a more like-minded religious community.

words.definition: adjective: lecherous; sexually perverted
words.example: Lolita is a challenging novel for many, not necessarily because of the elevated prose style but because of the depravity of the main character, Humbert Humbert, who, as an old, lascivious man, lusts after a girl.

words.definition: adjective: prone to outbursts of temper; easily angered
words.example: While a brilliant lecturer, Mr. Dawson came across as choleric and unapproachable—very rarely did students come to his office hours.

words.definition: adjective: produced by, or characterized by internal dissension
words.example: The controversial bill proved factious, as dissension even within parties resulted

words.definition: noun: critical explanation or analysis, especially of a text
words.example: The Bible is fertile ground for exegesis—over the past five centuries there have been as many interpretations as there are pages in the Old Testament.

words.definition: adjective: done routinely and with little interest or care
words.example: The short film examines modern perfunctory cleaning rituals such as washing dishes, doing laundry and tooth-brushing.

words.definition: adjective: having a fierce, savage nature
words.example: Standing in line for six hours, she became progressively truculent, yelling at DMV employees and elbowing other people waiting in line.

words.definition: adjective: unfavorable; inconvenient
words.example: Some professors find teaching untoward as having to prepare for lectures and conduct office hours prevents them from focusing on their research.

words.definition: adjective: intricate and complex
words.example: Getting a driver’s license is not simply a matter of taking a test; the regulations and procedures are so byzantine that many have found themselves at the mercy of the Department of Motor Vehicles.

words.definition: verb: to make peace with
words.example: His opponents believed his gesture to be conciliatory, yet as soon as they put down their weapons, he unsheathed a hidden sword.

words.definition: adjective: intolerable, difficult to endure
words.example: Chester always tried to find some area in which he excelled above others; unsurprisingly, his co-workers found him insufferable and chose to exclude him from daily luncheons out.

words.definition: noun: the lowest point
words.example: For many pop music fans, the rap– and alternative-rock–dominated 90s were the nadir of musical expression.

words.definition: adjective: hasty or rash
words.example: Instead of conducting a thorough investigation after the city hall break-in, the governor acted precipitately, accusing his staff of aiding and abetting the criminals.

words.definition: adjective: lazy and irresponsible
words.example: Two years after graduation, Charlie still lived with his parents and had no job, becoming more feckless with each passing day.

words.definition: noun: an outcast
words.example: The once eminent scientist, upon being found guilty of faking his data, has become a pariah in the research community.

words.definition: verb: to bully or intimidate
words.example: The boss’s hectoring manner put off many employees, some of whom quit as soon as they found new jobs.

words.definition: verb: to eliminate completely
words.example: When I turned 18, all of the shoplifting and jaywalking charges were expunged from my criminal record.

words.definition: noun: an eager willingness to do something
words.example: The first three weeks at his new job, Mark worked with such alacrity that upper management knew it would be giving him a promotion.

words.definition: adjective: done diligently and carefully
words.example: An avid numismatist, Harold sedulously amassed a collection of coins from over 100 countries—an endeavor that took over fifteen years across five continents.

words.definition: adjective: cautious, suspiciously reluctant to do something
words.example: Having received three speeding tickets in the last two months, Jack was chary of driving at all above the speed limit, even on a straight stretch of highway that looked empty for miles ahead.

words.definition: noun: a person who thinks their country is always right and who is in favor of aggressive acts against other countries
words.example: In the days leading up to war, a nation typically breaks up into the two opposing camps: doves, who do their best to avoid war, and jingoists, who are only too eager to wave national flags from their vehicles and vehemently denounce those who do not do the same.

words.definition: noun: change in one’s circumstances, usually for the worse
words.example: Even great rulers have their vicissitudes—massive kingdoms have diminished overnight, and once beloved kings have faced the scorn of angry masses.

words.definition: adjective: weighed-down; moving slowly
words.example: Laden with 20 kilograms of college text books, the freshman moved ponderously across the campus.

words.definition: adjective: dull and lacking imagination
words.example: Unlike the talented artists in his workshop, Paul had no such bent for the visual medium, so when it was time for him to make a stained glass painting, he ended up with a prosaic mosaic.

words.definition: noun: misconduct or wrongdoing (especially by a public official)
words.example: Not even the mayor’s trademark pearly-toothed grin could save him from charges of malfeasance: while in power, he’d been running an illegal gambling rink in the room behind his office.

words.definition: verb: to help pay the cost of, either in part or full
words.example: In order for Sean to attend the prestigious college, his generous uncle helped defray the excessive tuition with a monthly donation.

words.definition: verb: to weaken (in terms of intensity); to taper off/become thinner.
words.example: Her animosity towards Bob attenuated over the years, and she even went so far as to invite him to her party.

words.definition: adjective: smooth and sweet-sounding
words.example: Chelsea’s grandmother thought Franz Schubert’s music to be the most mellifluous ever written; Chelsea demurred, and to her grandmother’s chagrin, would blast Rihanna on the home stereo speakers.

words.definition: adjective: overly emotional and sad
words.example: Just as those who were alive during the 70’s are mortified that they once cavorted about in bellbottoms, many who lived during the 80’s are now aghast at the maudlin pop songs they used to enjoy—really, just what exactly is a total eclipse of the heart?

words.definition: noun: a grouchy, surly person
words.example: Since Uncle Mike was the family curmudgeon, each Thanksgiving he was plied with copious amounts of wine, in the hope that he would become less grouchy.

words.definition: adjective: likely to lean towards a controversial view
words.example: Because political mudslinging has become a staple of the 24-hour media cycle, most of us, despite protestations to the contrary, are tendentious on many of today’s pressing issues.

words.definition: noun: abusive or denunciatory language
words.example: The Internet has unleashed the invectives in many of us; many people post stinging criticism on the comments section underneath newspaper articles or YouTube videos.

words.definition: adjective: readily taking on different roles; versatile
words.example: Peter Sellers was truly a protean actor—in Doctor Strangelove he played three very different roles: a jingoist general, a sedate President and a deranged scientist.

words.definition: verb: to persuade somebody that his/her belief is not valid
words.example: As a child, I was quickly disabused of the notion that Santa Claus was a rotund benefactor of infinite largess—one night I saw my mother diligently wrapping presents and storing them under our Christmas tree.

words.definition: adjective: to be overly theatrical
words.example: Though she received a B- on the test, she had such a histrionic outburst that one would have thought that she’d been handed a death sentence.

words.definition: noun: a traitor
words.example: History looks unfavorably upon quislings; indeed they are accorded about the same fondness as Nero—who watched his city burn down while playing the violin.

words.definition: noun: exaltation to divine status; the highest point of development
words.example: As difficult as it is to imagine, the apotheosis of Mark Zuckerberg’s career, many believe, is yet to come.

words.definition: adjective: extremely optimistic
words.example: Even in the midst of a lousy sales quarter, Debbie remained Pollyannaish, never losing her shrill voice and wide smile, even when prospective customers hung up on her.

words.definition: verb: to remove objectionable material
words.example: The censor expurgated every reference to sex and drugs, converting the rapper's raunchy flow into a series of bleeps.

words.definition: adjective: bossy and domineering
words.example: My sister used to peremptorily tell me to do the dishes, a chore I would either do perfunctorily or avoid doing altogether.

words.definition: adjective: fallen into a state of ignorance
words.example: Far from being a period of utter benightedness, The Medieval Ages produced some great works of theological speculation.

words.definition: verb: to placate or appease
words.example: The two sons, plying their angry father with cheesy neckties for Christmas, were hardly able to propitiate him – the father already had a drawer full of ones he had never worn before or ever planned to.

words.definition: adjective: artificial; not natural
words.example: The defendant’s story was largely factitious and did not accord with eyewitness testimonies

words.definition: verb: to make objections while pleading
words.example: The mothers of the kidnapped victims remonstrated to the rogue government to release their children, claiming that the detention violated human rights.

words.definition: verb: to criticize very harshly
words.example: Entrusted with the prototype to his company’s latest smartphone, Larry, during a late night karaoke bout, let the prototype slip into the hands of a rival company—the next day Larry was excoriated, and then fired.

words.definition: noun: a force that cannot be stopped
words.example: Napoleon was considered a juggernaut until he decided to invade Russia in winter; after which, his once indomitable army was decimated by cold and famine.

words.definition: verb: to criticize harshly; to berate
words.example: Jason had dealt with disciplinarians before, but nothing prepared him for the first week of boot camp, as drill sergeants vituperated him for petty oversights such as forgetting to double knot the laces on his boots.

words.definition: adjective: to be deliberately teasing
words.example: The baroness was arch, making playful asides to the townspeople; yet because they couldn't pick up on her dry humor, they thought her supercilious.

words.definition: adjective: wildly idealistic; impractical
words.example: For every thousand startups with quixotic plans to be the next big name in e-commerce, only a handful ever become profitable.

words.definition: noun: joy from watching the suffering of others
words.example: From his warm apartment window, Stanley reveled in schadenfreude as he laughed at the figures below, huddled together in the arctic chill.

words.definition: adjective: to be biased against due to envy or prejudice
words.example: Shelly was jaundiced towards Olivia; though the two had once been best friends, Olivia had become class president, prom queen, and, to make matters worse, the girlfriend of the one boy Shelly liked.

words.definition: adjective: describing a victory that comes at such a great cost that the victory is not worthwhile
words.example: George W. Bush’s win in the 2000 election was in many ways a pyrrhic victory: the circumstances of his win alienated half of the U.S. population.

words.definition: verb: to defraud or swindle
words.example: The so-called magical diet cure simply ended up mulcting Maria out of hundreds of dollars, but did nothing for her weight.

words.definition: verb: to limit or qualify a statement; to avoid making a direct statement
words.example: When asked why he had decided to buy millions of shares at the very moment the tech company's stock soared, the CEO hedged, mentioning something vague about gut instinct.

words.definition: noun: something that has been changed numerous times but on which traces of former iterations can still be seen
words.example:
The downtown was a palimpsest of the city’s checkered past: a new Starbucks had opened up next to
an abandoned, shuttered building, and a freshly asphalted road was inches away from a pothole large enough to swallow a small dog.

words.definition: verb: to manipulate voting districts in order to favor a particular political party
words.example: Years ago, savvy politicians had gerrymandered the city center to ensure their re-election.

words.definition: adjective: related to fashion or clothes
words.example: Monte was astute at navigating the world of finance; sartorially, however, he was found wanting—he typically would attempt to complement his beige tie with a gray suit and white pants.

words.definition: noun: a strict disciplinarian
words.example:
The job seemed perfect to Rebecca, until she found out that her boss was a total martinet; after each project the boss would come by to scrutinize—and inevitably criticize—every little detail of the work 
Rebecca had done.

words.definition: adjective: to have a limited outlook or understanding
words.example: In gambling, the blinkered addict is easily influenced by past successes and/or past failures, forgetting that the outcome of any one game is independent of the games that preceded it.

words.definition: noun: the confusion of a word with another word that sounds similar
words.example: Whenever I looked glum, my mother would offer to share "an amusing antidote" with me—an endearing malapropism of "anecdote" that never failed to cheer me up.

words.definition: adjective: having clarity in terms of expression
words.example: Her limpid prose made even the most recondite subjects accessible to all.

words.definition: adjective: lacking money; poor
words.example: In extremely trying times, even the moderately wealthy, after a few turns of ill-fortune, can become impecunious.

words.definition: adjective: dull; lacking flavor
words.example: Although many top chefs have secured culinary foam's popularity in haute cuisine, Waters criticizes it for being jejune and unfilling.

words.definition: adjective: easily excused or forgiven; pardonable
words.example: His traffic violations ran the gamut from the venial to the egregious—on one occasion he simply did not come to a complete stop; another time he tried to escape across state lines at speeds in excess of 140 mph.

words.definition: noun: a person who has suddenly become wealthy, but not socially accepted as part of a higher class
words.example: The theater was full of parvenus who each thought that they were surrounded by true aristocrats.

words.definition: adjective: trifling or petty (a person)
words.example: English teachers are notorious for being picayune; however, the English language is so nuanced and sophisticated that often such teachers are not being contrary but are only adhering to the rules.

words.definition: noun: a confusing and potentially embarrassing situation
words.example: The chef cook-off featured one gourmand who had the unfortunate distinction of mixing the wrong broths, creating an imbroglio that diners would not soon forget.

words.definition: noun: a person who indulges in luxury
words.example: Despite the fact that he’d maxed out fifteen credit cards, Max was still a sybarite at heart: when the police found him, he was at a $1,000 an hour spa in Manhattan, getting a facial treatment.

words.definition: verb: to curse and hiss at
words.example: Though the new sitcom did decently in the ratings, the critic execrated the show, saying that it was nothing more than a terrible pastiche of tired clichés and canned laughter.

words.definition: noun: calmness or poise in difficult situations
words.example: The hostage negotiator exhibited a sangfroid that oftentimes was more menacing than the sword at his throat, or the gun at his head.

words.definition: noun: a person who has recently reached a position of power; a social climber
words.example: The city center was aflutter with arrivistes who tried to outdo one another with their ostentatious sports cars and chic evening dress.

words.definition: adjective: terribly evil
words.example: For fans of the Harry Potter series, the fell Lord Voldemort, who terrorized poor Harry for seven lengthy installments, has finally been vanquished by the forces of good—unless, that is, JK Rowling decides to come out of retirement.

words.definition: adjective: illusive; unreal
words.example: Those suffering from malaria fall into a feverish sleep, their world a whirligig of phantasmagoria; if they recover, they are unsure of what actually took place and what was simply a product of their febrile imaginations.

words.definition: adjective: to be moralizing, usually in a pompous sense
words.example: The old man, casting his nose up in the air at the group of adolescents, intoned sententiously, “Youth is wasted on the young.”

words.definition: adjective: irritable; always angry
words.example: Rex was bilious all morning, and his face would only take on a look of contentedness when he’d had his morning cup of coffee.

words.definition: noun: greed for money
words.example: Some people believe that amassing as much wealth as possible is the meaning to life—yet they often realize that cupidity brings anything but happiness.

words.definition: adjective: filled with courage or valor
words.example: For its raid on the Bin Laden’s compound in Abbottabad, Seal Team Six has become, for many Americans, the embodiment of mettle.

words.definition: adjective: excessively mournful
words.example: At the funeral, lugubrious songs filled the small church.

words.definition: noun: a socially awkward or tactless act
words.example: Mother Anna was always on guard against any solecism from her children and scolded them immediately if any of them talked out of place in public.

words.definition: noun: a summary (think of recap)
words.example: Every point of the professors lesson was so clear that the students felt his concluding recapitulation was not necessary.

words.definition: adjective: uncooperative, not willing to give up information
words.example: The teacher demanded to know who broke the window while he was out of the room, but the students understandably were unforthcoming.

words.definition: adjective: lacking energy and vigor
words.example: After three straight shows, the lead actress gave an anemic performance the fourth night, barely speaking loudly enough for those in the back rows to hear.

words.definition: adjective: inspiring fear or awe
words.example: On television basketball players don't look that tall, but when you stand in front of a seven-foot tall NBA player, he is truly redoubtable.

words.definition: adjective: widely known and esteemed; having or conferring glory
words.example: Einstein was possibly the most illustrious scientist in recent history.

words.definition: adjective: having good judgement and acute insight
words.example: Steve Jobs is surely one of the most sagacious CEOs, making Apple one of the most recognizable and valuable companies in the world.

words.definition: adjective: (of a person) not doing one's duties
words.example: The teacher was derelict in her duties because she hadn't graded a single student paper in three weeks.

words.definition: noun: the quality of innocence
words.example: I, personally, found the artlessness of her speech charming.

words.definition: adjective: puffed up with vanity
words.example: The dictator was known for his grandiloquent speeches, puffing his chest out and using big, important-sounding words.

words.definition: adjective: marked by courage and determination
words.example: Some scouts initially doubted Pedroia because of his short stature, but he is a plucky player, surprising everyone with his boundless energy and fierce determination.

words.definition: adjective: being on the point of death; declining rapidly losing all momentum in progress
words.example: Whether you like it or not, jazz as a genre is moribund at best, possibly already dead.

words.definition: noun: fearless daring
words.example: No child has the temerity to go in the rundown house at the end of the street and see if it is haunted.

words.definition: adjective: ominously prophetic
words.example: When the captain and more than half the officers were sick on the very first night of the voyage, many of the passengers felt this was portentous, but the rest of the voyage continued without any problems.

words.definition: adjective: excessively flattering toward someone's life or work
words.example: Most accounts of Tiger Woods's life were hagiographic, until, that is, his affairs made headlines.

words.definition: noun: an office that involves minimal duties
words.example: The position of Research Director is a sinecure: the job entails almost no responsibilities, nor does the person in that position have to answer to anyone.

words.definition: verb: wander aimlessly
words.example: Max liked to maunder down by the seaside and pick up whatever sea shells he would stumble upon.

words.definition: noun: lack of concern
words.example: Surprisingly, Hank had become a high-powered CEO; his high school friends remembered him as "Hanky Panky", who shrugged off each failed class with insouciance.

words.definition: noun: a statement made about the future
words.example: When the Senator was asked about where the negotiations would lead, he said that any guess he could make would be an unreliable prognostication.

words.definition: noun: the state of being first in importance
words.example: The primacy of Apple Computers is not guaranteed, as seen in the recent lawsuits and weak growth.

words.definition: noun: integrity, strong moral principles
words.example: The ideal politician would have the probity to lead, but reality gravely falls short of the ideal of morally upright leaders.

words.definition: noun: something that soothes or relieves pain
words.example: Muzak, which is played in department stores, is intended to be an anodyne, but is often so cheesy and over-the-top that customers become irritated.

words.definition: noun: deceitfulness, pretending to want one thing but interested in something else
words.example: A life of espionage is one of duplicity: an agent must pretend to be a totally different person than who she or he actually is.

words.definition: verb: beg persistently and urgently
words.example: After weeks of importuning the star to meet for a five-minute interview, the journalist finally got what she wanted.

words.definition: adjective: harsh or corrosive in tone
words.example: While the teacher was more moderate in her criticism of the other student's papers, she was vitriolic toward Peter's paper, casting every flaw in the harshest light.

words.definition: noun: an outward or token appearance or form that is deliberately misleading
words.example: While the banker maintained a semblance of respectability in public, those who knew him well were familiar with his many crimes.

words.definition: noun: audacious (even arrogant) behavior that you have no right to
words.example: The skateboarders acted with effrontery, skating through the church grounds and spray-painting signs warning trespassers.

words.definition: verb: draw back, as with fear or pain
words.example: Craig always claimed to be a fearless outdoorsman, but when the thunderstorm engulfed the valley, he quailed at the thought of leaving the safety of his cabin.

words.definition: adjective: biting and caustic in thought, manner, or style
words.example: While Phil frequently made mordant remarks about company policy overall, he always was considerably gentler in discussing any person in particular.

words.definition: verb: be a mystery or bewildering to
words.example: Mary's behavior completely flummoxes me: I never have any idea what her motivations might be.

words.definition: verb: edit by omitting or modifying parts considered indelicate
words.example: To receive an R rating, the entire movie was bowdlerized because it contained so much violence and grotesque subject matter.

words.definition: verb: ridicule with satire
words.example: Mark Twain understood that lampooning a bad idea with humor was the most effective criticism.

words.definition: verb: attribute (responsibility or fault) to something
words.example: He imputed his subpar performance on the test to a combination of stress and poor sleep.

words.definition: adjective: acutely insightful and wise
words.example: Many modern observers regard Eisenhower as perspicacious, particularly in his accurate prediction of the growth of the military.

words.definition: adjective: expressing praise or approval
words.example: Although it might not be her best work, Hunter's new novel has received generally approbatory reviews.

words.definition: noun: a sudden revelation or moment of insight
words.example: Gary one day had an epiphany that he was a people person; he promptly quit his factory job and began working as a salesman.

words.definition: adjective: marked by precise accordance with details
words.example: The colonel was so punctilious about enforcing regulations that men feel compelled to polish even the soles of their shoes.

words.definition: noun: any long and tedious account of something
words.example: Mr. Rogers spoke to a Senate committee and did not give a litany of reasons to keep funding the program, but instead, appealed to the basic human decency of all present.

words.definition: noun: a feeling of anger caused by being offended
words.example: Since he was so in love with her, he took umbrage at her comments, even though she had only meant to gently tease him.

words.definition: adjective: careful in regard to your own interests; providing carefully for the future
words.example: In a move that hardly could be described as provident, Bert spent his entire savings on a luxurious cruise, knowing that other bills would come due a couple months later.

words.definition: noun: boring verbosity
words.example: I loved my grandfather dearly, but his prolixity would put me to sleep, regardless of the topic.

words.definition: noun: a flamboyant deceiver; one who attracts customers with tricks or jokes
words.example: You may call him a "motivational speaker," but I call him a charlatan--he doesn't have any idea what he's really talking about.

words.definition: verb: enthusiastically acclaim or celebrate something
words.example: Many college superstar athletes are hailed as the next big thing, but then flop at the professional level.

words.definition: verb: relinquish possession or control over
words.example: Eventually, all parents must cede control of their growing childrens' educations and allow their offspring some autonomy.

words.definition: noun: a person skilled in telling anecdotes
words.example: Jude is entertaining, but he is no raconteur: beyond the handful of amusing stories he has memorized, he has absolutely no spontaneous story-telling ability.

words.definition: adjective: relating to or involving money
words.example: The defendant was found guilty and had to serve a period of community service as well as pay pecuniary damages to the client.

words.definition: verb: hold spellbound
words.example: She was so enthralled by the movie that she never heard people screaming, "Fire! Fire!" in the neighboring theater.

words.definition: verb: give instructions to or direct somebody to do something with authority
words.example: The government agency enjoined the chemical company to clean up the hazardous dump it had created over the years.

words.definition: noun: a socially awkward or tactless act
words.example: In a famous gaffe, Vice President Quayle attempted to correct the spelling of a grade school student, only to find that the child was correct.

words.definition: adjective: made more subtle or refined
words.example: Jack's vulgar jokes were not so successful in the rarefied environment of college professors.

words.definition: adjective: remarkably appropriate
words.example: For a writer with such quick wit, Jonathan Swift has a rather apposite name.

words.definition: noun: an exemption from a rule or obligation
words.example: Since her father is a billionaire, she is given dispensation from many of the school's policies.

words.definition: noun: the final resolution of the many strands of a literary or dramatic work; the outcome of a complex sequence of events
words.example: At the denouement of the movie, all questions were answered, and the true identity of the robber was revealed.

words.definition: adjective: powerful
words.example: Over the years of service, and quite to his surprise, he became a puissant advisor to the community.

words.definition: adjective: showing inappropriate levity
words.example: Although Sam was trying to honor Mark's sense of humor, many found it quite flippant that he wore a comic nose and glasses mask to Mark's funeral.

words.definition: verb: to make accustomed to something unpleasant
words.example: Three years of Manhattan living has inured her to the sound of wailing sirens; she could probably sleep through the apocalypse.

words.definition: adjective: impossible to deny or disprove
words.example: Scientists are searching for irrefutable evidence that some form of life existed on mars at some point in its history.

words.definition: noun: mutual accusations
words.example: The two brothers sat and cried, pointing fingers and making elaborate recriminations of the other's guilt

words.definition: verb: to hold back  the progress of something
words.example: Bad weather has hobbled rescue efforts, making it difficult for crews to find bodies in the wreckage.

words.definition: adjective: necessarily or demonstrably true; impossible to deny or disprove
words.example: Unless you can provide incontrovertible evidence, I will remain skeptical.

words.definition: adjective: characterized by undue haste and lack of thought or deliberation
words.example: Herbert is rarely impetuous, but on the spur of the moment, he spent thousands of dollars on a motorcycle today.

words.definition: adjective: must be kept sacred
words.example: While the literary critic subjected most of the classics to the harshest reviews, he regarded Cervantes as inviolate, and had nothing but praise for him.

words.definition: adjective: (of theories etc) incapable of being defended or justified
words.example: With the combination of Kepler's brilliant theories and Galileo's telescopic observations, the old geocentric theory became untenable to most of the educated people in Europe.

words.definition: verb: fit together tightly, as if by means of an interlocking joint
words.example: Although Darwin's evolution and Mendel's genetics were developed in isolation from one another, they dovetail very well.

words.definition: adjective: offensively self-assured or given to exercising unwarranted power
words.example: Though she was only a third grade teacher, Ms. Martinet was magisterial in dealing with her class, lording over them like a queen.

words.definition: verb: make rigid and set into a conventional pattern
words.example: Even as a young man, Bob had some bias against poor people, but during his years in social services, his bad opinions ossified into unshiftable views.

words.definition: noun: speed, rapidity
words.example: We aim to respond to customers' questions with celerity and accuracy, with no longer than a 24 hour wait time.

words.definition: noun: something intended to misrepresent the true nature of an activity
words.example: Finally deciding to abandon all subterfuge, Arthur revealed to Cindy everything about his secret affair over the past two years.

words.definition: adjective: coming across as uninterested or unconcerned; overly casual
words.example: The twenty-somethings at the coffee shop always irked Sheldon, especially the way in which they acted nonchalantly towards everything, not even caring when Sheldon once spilled his mocha on them.

words.definition: adjective: humorously vulgar
words.example: The speaker was famous for his ribald humor, but the high school principal asked him to keep the talk G-rated when he spoke to the student body.

words.definition: adjective: not able to work, survive, or succeed (also spelled inviable).
words.example: The plan was obviously unviable considering that it lead to complete environmental destruction in the river valley.

words.definition: adjective: unsparing and uncompromising in discipline or judgment; practicing great self-denial
words.example: After losing everything in a fire, Tim decided to live in spartan conditions, sleeping on the floor and owning as little furniture as possible.

words.definition: adjective: not given careful consideration
words.example: Marty was improvident, never putting money aside for the future but spending it on decorating the interior of his home.
